title: exo01-sim — Architecture
subtitle: Built from a scan of exo01/, app.py, web/, scripts/, tests/, configs/, scenarios/, data/, results/ (v1.2.1, 30 Oct 2026)
summary: Three layers: a pure-Python calculation package (exo01/: hydrostatics → still-water equilibrium → BEM hydrodynamics → linear and time-domain wave response, with the Hydronaute as a second moored body), a Flask API (app.py) that runs the long BEM/optimisation jobs in separate processes, and a vendored three.js browser UI (web/). Study scripts (scripts/) call the same package and write the committed results (mooring, stability, optimisation, website figures). Every illustrative result carries the label 'Exploratory — assumed geometry and mass distribution'.

clusters.label: Core — second body, mooring elements, propulsion

nodes.label: 3D interface
nodes.description: Single-page three.js viewer: loads the EXO and boat GLBs, draws floats, people, batteries, mooring elements (line blue / fender cyan / strut grey) and the waterline; edits components, people, lines and propulsion; shows still-water results, wave plots and job progress.
decisions: No build step: three.js is vendored under web/vendor so the app runs offline from start_windows.bat.
The UI never computes physics — every number comes from /api/*; results are re-rendered from the server payload.
window.__exo exposes camera/scene for the headless render script.

nodes.label: three.js vendored
nodes.description: Pinned three.js build plus loaders/controls used by the viewer; the reference GLBs are served by app.py.

nodes.label: Flask API
nodes.description: HTTP surface: /api/evaluate (still water, synchronous), /api/wave, /api/snatch, /api/irregular, /api/timestep_check (wave response from cached BEM), /api/hydro and /api/optimise (queued jobs), /api/compare, /api/export, scenario save/load, GLB files.
decisions: Still-water evaluation is synchronous (< 1 s, cached tessellation); anything with BEM goes through the job queue so the server never blocks.
Wave endpoints use cache_only BEM lookups with pose reuse (POSE_TOL tiers) — if no cached pose is close enough they tell the UI to run /api/hydro first.

nodes.label: Job runner
nodes.description: Scheduler thread in app.py starts one multiprocessing 'spawn' Process per BEM or optimisation job; exo01/jobs.py is the process entry point and writes progress and result JSON files that the API polls.
decisions: Separate process, not thread: Capytaine BEM is CPU-bound and would freeze the Flask server under the GIL.
Progress callbacks (fraction, message, ETA) are written to a file so the UI progress bar survives a page reload.

nodes.label: Launchers
nodes.description: Double-click launchers: create/reuse a venv, pip install, start app.py on :8050 and open the browser; update_windows.bat is a git pull (environment and BEM cache kept).

nodes.label: EXO-01 reference pkg
nodes.description: Revision-3 reference package: STEP + GLB geometry, parameters.json, mass metadata and validation reports; exo01/reference.py parses and audits it (units, extents, float positions).
decisions: Geometry is read, never edited: the floats are Flofiz pontoons modelled from the plan ('mesures approximatives'); masses are user-reported or user-estimated and tagged as such.

nodes.label: Renaud 8000 package
nodes.description: Hydronaute hull as a station table → closed hull envelope PROXY (exo01/boat.py); whole-boat mass metadata; GLB for display.
decisions: The hull is a proxy from stations, not a survey: the boat's own hydrostatics are indicative and labelled as such.

nodes.label: Configs & scenarios
nodes.description: configs/baseline.json keeps unknown inputs null (reports 'not computed'); configs/illustrative.json fills them with labelled assumptions and the line presets; scenarios/*.json are overrides (batteries moved, occupants, with_hydronaute). exo01/config.py resolves overrides → one fully-resolved config and validates it.
decisions: Baseline vs illustrative is the claim-discipline mechanism: a number only exists if its inputs exist.
scripts/make_configs.py regenerates both configs from the reference packages, so geometry edits happen in one place.

nodes.label: Mass model
nodes.description: Mass, centre of mass and inertia tensor from explicitly assigned component properties (point, solid/shell box, cylinder shell); people as point masses on an occupied surface; raises MissingInput instead of guessing.

nodes.label: Hydrostatics
nodes.description: Closed triangulated surfaces (CapsuleX proxy, FlofizX pontoon, imported MeshSurface) clipped by z = 0; exact wet volume, centroid and waterplane integrals of the assembly at any heel/trim.
decisions: Exact integrals on triangles rather than tabulated hydrostatics so arbitrary heel/trim and asymmetric floats are handled with one code path.

nodes.label: Still-water equilibrium
nodes.description: Newton solve for draft, heel and trim (zero net force/moment), exact restoring matrix, initial stability (GM-like measures), freeboards per float and deck point, NoEquilibrium with the best balance point when none exists.

nodes.label: evaluate()
nodes.description: The orchestrator for one resolved config: mass → equilibrium → stability → freeboards → (if host boat) coupled equilibrium and clearances → propulsion speed; also builds the ResponseModel from BEM data (hydro_for / build_response).
decisions: Tessellation is cached per config and the previous equilibrium seeds the next Newton solve (warm_key) — that is what makes the UI feel interactive.

nodes.label: BEM (Capytaine)
nodes.description: Added mass, radiation damping and exact-heading wave excitation on an (omega, heading) grid for one body or N bodies in a common world frame; internal free-surface lid for irregular frequencies; resonant gap-band detection between float rows.
decisions: BEM is computed about each body's CAD origin (COM-independent) and transformed exactly to the COM afterwards, so moving a battery never invalidates the cache.
Cache by pose signature with tiered tolerance (POSE_TOL 'near' / POSE_TOL_COARSE 'approximate'): a nearby pose is reused and flagged, not recomputed.

nodes.label: Wave response
nodes.description: Linear frequency-domain RAOs for 6 or 12 DOF (EXO + boat) with line/fender/strut stiffness, regular and irregular (JONSWAP) waves, deck accelerations and relative-motion points; time-domain RK4 check at fixed coefficients; line_snatch_check replaces the linear elements by unilateral laws (tension-only, compression-only, bilateral) and reports peaks, slack fraction and snatch ratio.
decisions: Damping = radiation + an assumed fraction of critical (5 %, 10 % boat roll/pitch): there is no viscous model, and the assumption is stated in every output.
Linear and time-domain results are always reported separately.

nodes.label: Coupled equilibrium
nodes.description: The Hydronaute as a second floating body: its own equilibrium, common-world poses, mooring elements with a kind (line +1 tension-only, fender −1 compression-only with signed penetration, strut 0 bilateral), active-set static solve of EXO + boat under thrust/tow, clearances (transom gap, propeller).
decisions: A 1 N/m centering spring is always on so fender-only arrangements have a defined sway/yaw reference.
Fender rest length L0 = Lnom + T0/k so preload is expressed the same way as line pretension.

nodes.label: Propulsion / tow
nodes.description: Quasi-static thrust → steady speed → forces on each body: ITTC-57 friction with form factor plus frontal pressure drag for the floats, boat resistance from the hull envelope; the external force callable the coupled solver uses for push and tow cases.
decisions: Every coefficient is an explicit, editable assumption in the config (no hidden hull-form data).

nodes.label: Design sweeps
nodes.description: Battery position (rear deck / float frame zones with upright obstacles) and mooring-line candidate sweeps using the real solvers and cached BEM; scoring is explicit and reported as 'highest-ranked under selected scoring'.

nodes.label: Mooring studies
nodes.description: run_mooring_study.py: arrangement × line stiffness × pretension (static moored/push/tow + three waves, linear and time domain); run_mooring_final.py: the 12 candidate arrangements (ropes + knees, four tubes, hybrids) at the converged settings. Read in docs/MOORING.md.

nodes.label: Stability sheet
nodes.description: run_stability_sheet.py: EXO-01 without the boat — load cases (empty, 4–6 persons, one side, zoned deck), heel/freeboard against ES-TRIN 19.03/19.04 readings, wind, deck-awash wave table, recommended layout cases, extra-float what-ifs.

nodes.label: Comparison, optimisation, verification
nodes.description: run_comparison.py (scenario table, with BEM), run_optimisation_report.py (battery zones), run_verification.py (checks against the reference packages: volumes, extents, symmetry, convergence), precompute_cache.py / prune_cache.py (BEM cache management).

nodes.label: Website package
nodes.description: render_website.py drives the running UI headlessly (Playwright) for 9 renders; draw_layout.py draws the recommended deck layout; docs/website holds the FR/EN article, figures.json and key_numbers.json with the origin of every quoted number.

nodes.label: BEM cache
nodes.description: Radiation / diffraction coefficients per (geometry signature, pose, grid) as .npz, indexed by pose_index.json; only indexed files are committed (prune_cache.py --apply --stage), everything else is git-ignored.
decisions: Committing the pruned cache means a fresh clone can run every wave endpoint on the illustrative scenarios without a 10-minute BEM.

nodes.label: Committed results
nodes.description: Markdown/JSON/CSV tables and PNG sketches written by the study scripts; local outputs (exports, jobs, ui) are not committed.

nodes.label: pytest suite
nodes.description: Unit and integration tests: hydrostatic integrals vs analytic shapes, equilibrium, mass, reference package parsing, BEM + response on small grids, two-body coupling, mooring element kinds (line/fender/strut laws), propulsion, jobs, API smoke.

nodes.label: Claim-discipline docs
nodes.description: ASSUMPTIONS.md (conventions, assumptions, limits, validation plan — §5e mooring elements), AUDIT.md (what the reference packages contain), docs/MOORING.md (study readings §1–7), docs/API.md, CHANGELOG.md.
decisions: Read AUDIT.md and ASSUMPTIONS.md before quoting any number — the README says so and the website article repeats the maturity label.

flows.label: Still water
flows.title: Editing a battery position in the UI (synchronous)
steps: The UI sends the base config name plus overrides (component positions, people, lines, thrust) to POST /api/evaluate.
config.resolve() merges overrides into a fully-resolved config and validates it (null inputs → 'not computed').
mass.items_from_config / mass_properties give M, COM and inertia; MissingInput stops the chain instead of guessing.
buoyancy builds the BuoyantAssembly (cached tessellation); equilibrium solves draft, heel, trim by Newton, seeded by the previous solve.
With the Hydronaute present, twobody.coupled_equilibrium solves both bodies with the mooring elements (active set) and propulsion forces.
The result dict (freeboards, stability, line tensions, clearances, speed) is rendered by the UI in < 1 s.
decisions: Nothing in this path touches the BEM, so it stays interactive; the label 'Exploratory' is attached by the server, not the UI.

flows.label: BEM job
flows.title: Computing hydrodynamics for a new pose (background process)
steps: POST /api/hydro queues a job; the scheduler thread spawns a Process running exo01.jobs.run_job.
hydro_job builds the immersed Capytaine meshes at the equilibrium pose (about the CAD origins), with an internal lid.
compute_hydro_bodies solves radiation for every omega and diffraction for every heading; progress (fraction, ETA) is written to a file.
Coefficients are stored as .npz in results/cache and registered in pose_index.json with the pose signature.
The UI polls /api/job/<id>; when done, wave endpoints find the pose (exact, 'near' or 'approximate' tier) and run instantly.
decisions: COM-independent BEM + pose tolerance tiers are why most UI edits never trigger a new BEM.

flows.label: Wave response
flows.title: A regular wave with tension-only mooring lines
steps: POST /api/wave (H, T, heading, damping) after a still-water evaluate.
analysis.hydro_for looks the BEM up in the cache (cache_only, pose reuse allowed) and build_response assembles the 12-DOF model with line/fender/strut stiffness.
ResponseModel.regular_wave returns RAOs, deck accelerations, relative motions (transom gap) and linear element tensions.
POST /api/snatch runs line_snatch_check: RK4 in time with unilateral element laws → peak loads, slack fraction, snatch ratio.
The UI plots both and labels linear vs time-domain separately.
decisions: Damping is radiation + an assumed fraction of critical; the assumption travels with the result.

flows.label: Mooring study
flows.title: From a sketch to results/mooring/final_comparison.md
steps: Candidate arrangements are built as element lists (kind, EXO point, boat point, k, T0) from the line presets in configs/illustrative.json.
For each: static moored / push / tow cases through evaluate() and the coupled solver; the push and tow loops must close (hard gate).
Three waves (beam 0.3 m, head 0.3 m, beam 0.5 m): linear response + time-domain snatch check from the cached BEM.
An explicit score (worst peak, slack, transom overlap, boat roll, static shift) ranks the candidates; weights are printed in the table.
Tables and sketches go to results/mooring/, the reading to docs/MOORING.md §7, the changelog entry to CHANGELOG.md.
decisions: Scripts import the same exo01 functions as the server — there is no second physics path to keep consistent.

matrices.title: API endpoints (app.py)
rows: still-water result (freeboards, stability, lines, clearances, propulsion)
RAOs, accelerations, relative motions, linear element loads
peaks, slack fraction, snatch ratio per element

matrices.title: Element kinds (exo01/twobody.py, response.py)
rows: tension only; slack when shorter than L0
compression only; signed penetration along the nominal axis
bilateral (rigid in the stiff limit, k 1 MN/m)

notes.text: One physics path: the UI, the API and every study script call the same exo01 functions; results differ only by inputs.
Claim discipline is structural: baseline config keeps unknowns null and reports 'not computed'; illustrative results carry the 'Exploratory' label from the server.
BEM cache is keyed by geometry signature and pose with two tolerance tiers; results flag 'pose_reuse' when an approximate pose was used.
No viscous or element damping anywhere: wave results use radiation damping + an assumed fraction of critical, so shock absorbers can only be modelled as stiffness.

The Hydronaute hull is a station-table proxy and EXO masses are user-reported/estimated: the registration sheet needs the measured light-ship weight and an inclining test before any number is a characteristic.
Long results (results/cache beyond pose_index.json, exports, jobs, ui renders) are git-ignored; prune_cache.py --apply --stage is the only way cache files enter the repo.
